question: Is the expected data volume high?
instructions: Judge whether users routinely work with more records than comfortably fit on one screen (roughly 50 or more at a time).

criteria.true: Users regularly face dozens to thousands of records
criteria.false: Users work with a handful of records at a time

question: Is comparison between records important?
instructions: Judge whether users need to compare values across multiple records side by side to do their primary task.

criteria.true: Users compare attributes across several records
criteria.false: Users look at one record at a time

question: Is filtering required?
instructions: Judge whether users need to narrow the set of records by attributes such as status, category, owner or date.

criteria.true: Users need to narrow records by attributes
criteria.false: Users can work with the full set without narrowing it

question: Is sorting required?
instructions: Judge whether users need to reorder records by an attribute such as amount, date or priority to find what matters.

criteria.true: Users need to reorder records by attributes
criteria.false: A single fixed order is sufficient

question: Do users need to search for specific records?
instructions: Judge whether users need to find a specific known record by name, id or text rather than by browsing.

criteria.true: Users look up specific known records
criteria.false: Users only browse or work through records in order

question: How much information per record must be visible at once?
instructions: Rate how many attributes of each record users need to see at a glance, without opening the record.
criteria: Low: one or two attributes such as a title and a status
High: six or more attributes compared at a glance

question: Are records primarily recognized visually?
instructions: Judge whether users identify records mainly by an image or visual preview (photos, thumbnails, designs) rather than by text and numbers.

criteria.true: Records are recognized by images or visual previews
criteria.false: Records are recognized by text and numbers

question: How is the data structured?
instructions: Pick the structure that best describes the main records users work with.

criteria.flat-independent-records: Independent records of the same kind, such as orders or tickets
criteria.nested-hierarchy: Records nested in parent/child levels, such as folders or org charts
criteria.ordered-stages: Records that move through ordered stages, such as a sales pipeline
criteria.time-ordered-events: Events that matter mainly by when they happened, such as an activity log

question: Is the primary task performed frequently?
instructions: Judge whether the primary task is performed daily or more often by the same users.

criteria.true: Performed daily or more often
criteria.false: Performed weekly or less often

question: Are bulk actions required?
instructions: Judge whether users need to apply the same action to several records at once.

criteria.true: Users apply one action to many records at once
criteria.false: Users act on one record at a time

question: Do users need record details without losing their place in the list?
instructions: Judge whether users repeatedly open one record's details and then return to the same position in a list of records.

criteria.true: Users inspect details and return to the list repeatedly
criteria.false: Users rarely need record details, or work on one record in depth

question: Is the task a multi-step process?
instructions: Judge whether completing the primary task requires several distinct steps that must happen in order.

criteria.true: The task has several ordered steps
criteria.false: The task is done in one place

question: Is the task dominated by data entry?
instructions: Judge whether users spend most of their time entering or editing information in fields, rather than reviewing it.

criteria.true: Mostly entering or editing information
criteria.false: Mostly reviewing or acting on existing information

question: Does the task include a long form?
instructions: Judge whether users must complete a form with more than about seven fields.

criteria.true: There is a form with more than about seven fields
criteria.false: Forms are short or absent

question: Do users monitor aggregate metrics?
instructions: Judge whether users need totals, trends or KPIs across many records, beyond the individual records themselves.

criteria.true: Totals, trends or KPIs matter to the task
criteria.false: Only individual records matter

question: Must users spot unusual or problematic records?
instructions: Judge whether an important part of the task is noticing records that are unusual, risky or violate a policy.

criteria.true: Spotting unusual or problematic records is important
criteria.false: All records are handled the same way

question: Does the workflow include destructive actions?
instructions: Judge whether users can take actions that delete, reject, cancel or otherwise discard work or data, or that are hard to reverse.

criteria.true: There are destructive or hard-to-reverse actions
criteria.false: All actions are safe and easily reversed

question: Can destructive actions be undone easily?
instructions: Judge whether the destructive actions in this workflow could be undone immediately by the same user without side effects on other people.

criteria.true: Destructive actions can be undone immediately with no side effects
criteria.false: Destructive actions notify others, trigger processes or cannot be undone

question: How costly is a user error?
instructions: Rate the consequence of a user making a mistake in this workflow.
criteria: Low: a minor inconvenience, easily corrected
Medium: wasted time or rework for the user or a colleague
High: money, legal, safety or trust consequences

question: How much time pressure are users under?
instructions: Rate how much time pressure users are under while performing the primary task.
criteria: Low: users can take their time
Medium: there are deadlines but no moment-to-moment pressure
High: users must act within seconds or minutes

question: How many distinct sections does this experience have?
instructions: Pick how many distinct top-level sections or areas users move between in this experience.

criteria.single-focused-screen: One focused screen with no separate sections
criteria.few-peer-sections: Two to five peer sections users switch between
criteria.many-deep-sections: More than five sections, or sections nested several levels deep

question: How do users choose among options?
instructions: Pick how users select among the options presented to them in forms or settings (not rows in a list).

criteria.no-option-selection: Users do not choose among options
criteria.one-of-several: Users pick exactly one option from a set
criteria.several-independent: Users can pick several independent options
criteria.on-off-setting: Users switch a single setting on or off

question: How many options do users choose from?
instructions: Pick how many options a typical selection offers.

criteria.more-than-fifteen-options: More than fifteen options, such as countries or people

question: Is mobile use likely?
instructions: Judge whether a meaningful share of users will do this task on a phone.

criteria.true: A meaningful share of use happens on phones
criteria.false: Use happens almost entirely on larger screens

question: Do action outcomes arrive later?
instructions: Judge whether the results of users' actions complete in the background or arrive after a delay, rather than instantly.

criteria.true: Outcomes complete in the background or after a delay
criteria.false: Outcomes are immediate

question: Which data presentation best fits the task?
instructions: Pick the presentation that best supports the primary task for these users and this data.

criteria.data-table: Rows and columns for scanning, comparing and sorting many structured records
criteria.card-grid: Visual cards for browsing records recognized by images or a few attributes
criteria.list: A simple vertical list of records with one or two attributes each
criteria.timeline: Records placed in time order to show when things happened
criteria.kanban: Columns of cards representing stages that records move through
criteria.chart: A visualization of aggregate values rather than individual records

question: Which overall layout best fits the task?
instructions: Pick the screen-level layout that best supports the primary task.

criteria.single-page: One scrolling page holding the whole task
criteria.multi-step: A sequence of screens completed in order
criteria.split-view: A list beside a detail pane, so records are inspected without leaving the list
criteria.dashboard: An overview of several summary widgets and entry points
criteria.detail-view: One record shown in full depth

question: Does the task involve paying?
instructions: Judge whether users pay, purchase, subscribe or enter payment details as part of this task.

criteria.true: Users pay or enter payment details
criteria.false: No payment is involved

question: Does the task involve signing in or signing up?
instructions: Judge whether this experience includes signing in, signing up, or recovering an account.

criteria.true: Users sign in, sign up or recover an account
criteria.false: No authentication is involved

question: Do first-time users need guidance before they get value?
instructions: Judge whether new users must set something up or learn key concepts before the product becomes useful to them.

criteria.true: New users need setup or guidance first
criteria.false: Users get value immediately without setup

question: Do users configure preferences or settings?
instructions: Judge whether a meaningful part of this experience is changing preferences, options or settings.

criteria.true: Users change preferences or settings
criteria.false: Settings are not part of this experience

question: Do users choose between alternatives by comparing features?
instructions: Judge whether users pick one of a few alternatives, such as plans or products, by comparing their features side by side.

criteria.true: Users compare a few alternatives feature by feature
criteria.false: Users do not choose between alternatives this way

question: Do users create, edit and delete records?
instructions: Judge whether users manage the full lifecycle of records: creating new ones, editing them and deleting them.

criteria.true: Users create, edit and delete records
criteria.false: Users only review or act on existing records

question: Do users often change one or two fields of existing records?
instructions: Judge whether users frequently correct or update a single attribute of a record, such as a status or a name, without editing the whole record.

criteria.true: Users frequently make small edits to single fields
criteria.false: Edits are rare or involve many fields at once

question: Must users enter values in specific formats?
instructions: Judge whether users must type values that follow a required format, such as dates, phone numbers, amounts or identifiers.

criteria.true: Users type values in required formats
criteria.false: Inputs are free text or chosen from options
